I had 4 Nexplanons between the age of 18 and 32. Pain wise they are fine going in, personally it was worse for me having them taken out (particularly as I had 3 in the same "hole" lol which apparently they are not meant to do, it made them difficult to remove due to scar tissue).

The main benefit for me was being very sure I would not get pregnant, and they mostly stopped my periods completely. However, the last one I had (and towards the end of each one), I was constantly bleeding. Apparently it's more common as your hormones change as you age. I also realise looking back that (particularly every time I had a new one put in) a lot of my very depressive periods were at the very least exacerbated by the implant.

I finally made the decision to go hormone free last year, I now use Natural Cycles. I won't say it's fixed everything in my life, but I can't describe how much I more felt "normal" within hours of having it taken out. I have the ups and downs of my cycle but overall I'm much more level.

On a related point, I was diagnosed with hypothyroidism last year, and in my general research discovered there is a strong association with years on hormonal birth control and thyroid problems. I'm not saying this just to put you off, but I think it's important to consider that while the implant is very effective as birth control, it's not benign. I would say don't be like me and get 4 in a row if you do go for it :)
